1/** @file math.hpp
2 * @brief GLSL-compatible scalar, vector and matrix operations for C++11.
3 *
4 * Vectors provide x/y/z/w component fields, indexed access, and writable
5 * swizzles. Color and texture-coordinate aliases are accessor functions in
6 * ordinary C++ code. Matrices use GLSL column-major order. The same types and
7 * functions are available to generated CPU kernels and application code.
8 *
9 * Floating-point precision and exceptional values depend on the implementation.
10 * Normalize nonzero vectors, invert nonsingular matrices and use valid shift
11 * counts. Keep signed arithmetic within its representable range and use
12 * nonnegative signed operands for left shifts to follow portable C++ rules.
13 * Resource element layout is defined by the buffer and image APIs separately.
14 */

190/** @brief A fixed-size array for GLSL local variables and function arguments.
191 * The size must be positive. Default construction initializes every element to
192 * its zero/default value.  component construction requires exactly N elements.
193 * Copy construction and assignment copy all elements. Use length() to query
194 * the element count and operator[] to select an element with a valid index.
195 * Resource ports define buffer and uniform memory layouts separately.
196 */
197template <class T, std::size_t N> class array { // Store a fixed number of values of one element type.
198    static_assert(N > 0, "GLSL fixed arrays require a positive size"); // Require at least one fixed-array element.
199    T elements_[N]; // Keep exactly N fixed-array elements.
200
201  public: // Expose the public math operations.
202    typedef T value_type; // Expose the element type to host code and templates.
203    static const std::size_t size_value = N; // Keep the fixed component count available at compile time.
204    /** @brief Return the number of array elements. */
205    static constexpr std::size_t length() { // Record the compile-time component rule.
206        return N; // Return the fixed number of available components.
207    } // Finish the length operation.
208    /** @brief Initialize every element to its zero/default value. */
209    array() : elements_() { // Initialize fixed-array storage from the supplied values.
210    } // Finish initializing the fixed array.
211    /** @brief Construct from exactly N scalar or aggregate element values. */
212    template <class... A> // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
213    explicit array(const A&... values) : elements_{static_cast<T>(values)...} { // Initialize fixed-array storage from the supplied values.
214        static_assert(sizeof...(A) == N, "array constructor element count mismatch"); // Require exactly one argument for each array element.
215    } // Finish initializing the fixed array.
216    /** @brief Initialize from a C++ brace list containing exactly N elements.
217     * A length mismatch throws std::invalid_argument.
218     */
219    array(std::initializer_list<T> values) : elements_() { // Initialize fixed-array storage from the supplied values.
220        if (values.size() != N) // Reject a brace list with the wrong element count.
221            throw std::invalid_argument("array initializer element count mismatch"); // Report an initializer length mismatch.
222        std::size_t i = 0; // Begin filling the first array element.
223        for (const T& value : values) // Read initializer values in their original order.
224            elements_[i++] = value; // Store the next brace-list element.
225    } // Finish initializing the fixed array.
226    /** @brief Read or modify element i.  i must be less than length(). */
227    T& operator[](std::size_t i) { // Provide this arithmetic or component access overload.
228        return elements_[i]; // Return the selected component with its original reference type.
229    } // Finish this operator overload.
230    const T& operator[](std::size_t i) const { // Provide this arithmetic or component access overload.
231        return elements_[i]; // Return the selected component with its original reference type.
232    } // Finish this operator overload.
233}; // Finish the array type description.
234template <class T, std::size_t N> const std::size_t array<T, N>::size_value; // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
235/** @brief Compare two arrays by comparing every element. */
236template <class T, std::size_t N> bool operator==(const array<T, N>& a, const array<T, N>& b) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
237    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) // Visit each component needed by this calculation.
238        if (!(a[i] == b[i])) // Stop when corresponding components differ.
239            return false; // Report that at least one component differs.
240    return true; // Report that every required component matched.
241} // Finish this operator overload.
242/** @brief Return true when any pair of corresponding elements differs. */
243template <class T, std::size_t N> bool operator!=(const array<T, N>& a, const array<T, N>& b) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
244    return !(a == b); // Return the component count or geometric length.
245} // Finish this operator overload.

870/** @brief Determinant using partial-pivot elimination. */
871template <class T, std::size_t N> T determinant(mat<T, N, N> a) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
872    T result(1); // Begin the determinant product with multiplicative identity.
873    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) { // Visit each component needed by this calculation.
874        std::size_t pivot = i; // Begin with the current row as the pivot candidate.
875        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) // Visit each matrix row.
876            if (std::abs(a[i][r]) > std::abs(a[i][pivot])) // Prefer the row with the larger pivot magnitude.
877                pivot = r; // Use the stronger row for the next pivot.
878        if (a[i][pivot] == T(0)) // Detect a singular column before division.
879            return T(0); // Compute the determinant with row pivoting.
880        if (pivot != i) { // Swap rows when a better pivot was found.
881            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
882                T temp = a[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
883                a[c][i] = a[c][pivot]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
884                a[c][pivot] = temp; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
885            } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
886            result = -result; // Reverse the determinant sign after a row exchange.
887        } // Finish handling this condition.
888        T diagonal = a[i][i]; // Save the pivot value before normalizing the row.
889        result *= diagonal; // Multiply the determinant by the next diagonal value.
890        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) { // Visit each matrix row.
891            T factor = a[i][r] / diagonal; // Find the amount of the pivot row to eliminate.
892            for (std::size_t c = i + 1; c < N; ++c) // Visit each matrix column.
893                a[c][r] -= factor * a[c][i]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
894        } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
895    } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
896    return result; // Return the completed result.
897} // Finish the determinant operation.
898/** @brief Inverse using partial-pivot Gauss-Jordan elimination.
899 * Singular input has undefined GLSL semantics.  the host returns quiet NaNs.
900 */
901template <class T, std::size_t N> mat<T, N, N> inverse(mat<T, N, N> a) { // Accept the matching input types and dimensions.
902    mat<T, N, N> out(T(1)); // Keep an independent value for the result or aliased inputs.
903    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) { // Visit each component needed by this calculation.
904        std::size_t pivot = i; // Begin with the current row as the pivot candidate.
905        for (std::size_t r = i + 1; r < N; ++r) // Visit each matrix row.
906            if (std::abs(a[i][r]) > std::abs(a[i][pivot])) // Prefer the row with the larger pivot magnitude.
907                pivot = r; // Use the stronger row for the next pivot.
908        if (a[i][pivot] == T(0)) { // Detect a singular column before division.
909            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) // Visit each matrix column.
910                out[c] = vec<T, N>(std::numeric_limits<T>::quiet_NaN()); // Store the computed component in the independent result.
911            return out; // Return the completed result.
912        } // Finish handling this condition.
913        if (pivot != i) // Swap rows when a better pivot was found.
914            for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
915                T temp = a[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
916                a[c][i] = a[c][pivot]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
917                a[c][pivot] = temp; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
918                temp = out[c][i]; // Save an entry while exchanging the two rows.
919                out[c][i] = out[c][pivot]; // Store the computed component in the independent result.
920                out[c][pivot] = temp; // Store the computed component in the independent result.
921            } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
922        T diagonal = a[i][i]; // Save the pivot value before normalizing the row.
923        for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
924            a[c][i] /= diagonal; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
925            out[c][i] /= diagonal; // Store the computed component in the independent result.
926        } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
927        for (std::size_t r = 0; r < N; ++r) // Visit each matrix row.
928            if (r != i) { // Handle the exceptional or boundary case before continuing.
929                T factor = a[i][r]; // Find the amount of the pivot row to eliminate.
930                for (std::size_t c = 0; c < N; ++c) { // Visit each matrix column.
931                    a[c][r] -= factor * a[c][i]; // Update this matrix entry during row elimination or exchange.
932                    out[c][r] -= factor * out[c][i]; // Subtract the pivot-row contribution from the inverse.
933                } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
934            } // Finish handling this condition.
935    } // Finish this component or matrix pass.
936    return out; // Return the completed result.
937} // Finish the inverse operation.
